transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, I hope I'm not overreacting or wasting your time—it's probably nothing major. But, well, what finally made me come in is that I've just been having a little trouble at work lately. 

I'm a receptionist, and I've started sort of... losing my place while I'm scheduling appointments, or when I'm setting up the lobby displays. It's not that I can't do the job, it's just that my mind kind of slips off track because I'm busy thinking about little things I might have overlooked. I usually pride myself on being really on top of everything, so it's a bit embarrassing to even admit I'm slipping up. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place for this kind of thing.
Do you find yourself worrying more than you used to about everyday things?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I know everyone has stress, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about normal life. But... yes, I guess I have been fretting more about just... ordinary things. 

Like, um, the work schedules, or keeping up with bills, or even just making travel plans. Sometimes I get so caught up on a tiny paperwork error at the front desk, just... feeling like if I make one small mix-up, it’s going to somehow snowball and turn into this much bigger problem. It sounds a little silly when I say it out loud, doesn't it? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you been avoiding any situations or tasks because of your worries?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try my best to just push through and get everything done, especially at work. I would hate to let anyone down or... or not do my part just because I'm feeling a little stressed. 

So I still do all the tasks I'm supposed to do, I just... I might just fret about them a little more while I'm doing them, I guess. I hope that's okay? I mean, I haven't noticed myself actually backing away from anything or hiding from situations, if that's what you mean. I always try to face things head-on so I don't cause an inconvenience for anyone else. Am I answering that right?
Has something upsetting or traumatic happened to you recently?

Oh, um... well... I don't know if I would use the word traumatic, because I know people go through much, much worse things, and I really don't want to sound dramatic. 

But... there was a situation about nine months ago. It's actually a little hard to even talk about because I'm so afraid of what you might think of me, and I really don't want you to get the wrong idea. There was this... this huge paperwork mix-up. And it somehow ended up with me having an overnight detention. 

I promise it was just a terrible misunderstanding! I've never been in any sort of trouble in my entire life, I always follow the rules. But ever since that happened, for the last nine months, I just haven't been able to shake this nervous feeling. That's when all this extra worrying really started. I hope you don't judge me for that? I know it sounds ridiculous to still be rattled by a mix-up after nine months, but... is it okay that I'm still bothered by it?
Do you find yourself avoiding talking or thinking about the paperwork mix-up and the detention?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I don't go out of my way to avoid it or anything. It's not like I can't talk about it... I'm talking about it right now, right? 

I guess I just try not to dwell on it too much because I don't want to be a bother or sound like I'm stuck in the past. I know I should just move on. But if someone asks, or if I need to explain it, I can. I just... I try to keep it to myself mostly, so I don't make anyone else uncomfortable. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you often feel sad or empty inside?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. Not sad or empty, no. I mean, everyone has a down day here and there, right? But I always try to keep a positive attitude, especially since I'm at the front desk at work. I would hate to let any negativity affect the people coming in or make anyone else's day harder. 

Mostly it's just that... that nervous, worried feeling I mentioned earlier. I don't really feel empty at all. I hope it's okay that I don't have that symptom? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need to figure this out. Am I doing okay so far?
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches, stomachaches, or tremors lately?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. No tremors or stomachaches, thankfully. And my head has been completely fine. I mean, physically, I feel pretty healthy, which I'm really grateful for! 

It's really just that... that worrying I was talking about. I hope that's alright? Like, I hope I'm not missing something I should be noticing, or making your job harder by not having the symptoms you're looking for. Is it normal to just have the nervous feelings without all those physical things?
Do you ever have memories or images of the detention that come into your mind without you intentionally thinking about them?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I don't get flashes of it or anything like that. I mean, once in a while it might cross my mind, but it doesn't just force its way in out of nowhere like a movie playing, if that makes sense. 

It's really just the regular everyday worrying that I get caught up in. I don't have those sudden images at all. I really hope I'm giving you the right kind of information. Is it okay that I don't have those kinds of memories? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to. Am I being helpful?
Do you feel anxious most of the time, even when there's no apparent reason to be anxious?

Well, um... yes, I suppose I do. I hope it doesn't sound silly, but I just find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things lately. Like... work schedules, or bills, or travel plans. Even little paperwork errors at the front desk. I get this feeling like... like one small mix-up could somehow turn into a much bigger problem, you know? 

I really try to keep a lid on it, of course, so I'm still doing a good job and being pleasant with everyone who walks in. But the worry is just sort of... there, a lot of the time, even when everything is technically fine. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what's going on.
Do you find yourself avoiding places or people that remind you of the detention?

Oh, um... no, I don't. I really don't avoid anyone or any places because of that. I still go to work and do my regular routine just like always. I try very hard to just keep moving forward and be reliable, you know? 

So, no, no avoiding things. I hope that's okay? I know you're asking about it, so I hope it's not a problem that I don't have that happening. I'm just trying to answer as honestly as I can so I can be helpful to you. Am I doing alright with these questions?
Has your worrying or nervous feeling been causing problems in your relationships or daily activities?

Well, um... I really try not to let it cause any problems. I mean, I'm still showing up every day and getting through my shifts, being as helpful as I can to everyone. I don't want to be a burden or anything. 

But, I suppose... well, scheduling appointments has been taking me a bit longer lately. I just find myself double-checking the dates and times over and over, just to be absolutely sure I didn't make a mistake. And... oh, I feel a bit silly admitting this, but I've had to redo parts of the lobby displays a few times. I just sort of lose track of what I was arranging because my mind is so busy worrying about everything else. 

It's nothing terrible, I promise! I'm still doing my job. I just... I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or anything. Is it normal to get a little distracted like that when you're feeling anxious? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Do you avoid talking about the detention with friends or family?

Oh, um... no, not really. I don't avoid talking about it. I mean, if my family or friends bring it up, I'll absolutely talk to them. I'd never want to make anyone feel awkward by shutting down the conversation or refusing to speak, you know? 

I just try to be open and answer whatever they want to know so I'm not making a fuss or making them worry about me. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just try to go along with whatever they want to talk about. Am I... am I giving you the kind of answers you need for this? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Has your worry been causing significant problems in your ability to function at work or in your personal relationships?

Well, um... I think we touched on this a little bit just a moment ago, but I really am trying my best to keep everything running smoothly. I don't want you to think I'm failing at my job or anything like that. I'm definitely still showing up every day and getting through my shifts. 

It's just... well, like I mentioned, the scheduling does take me a bit longer now because I feel like I have to double-check myself so much. I just want to be perfectly sure I haven't messed up anyone's appointments. And, um, there's the thing with the lobby displays... having to redo them because I lose track of what I'm doing when my mind starts racing. 

But I promise I always fix it! I always make sure it looks nice before anyone notices. It's not causing any *huge* problems, I hope. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the full picture without making it sound worse than it is. Am I doing okay?
Do you have memories of the detention that feel like they are stuck in your mind and you can't get rid of them?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I have memories like that. The detention, I mean, it was definitely stressful, but I don't feel like the memories are stuck in my head or anything. I don't have those kinds of flashbacks or intrusive thoughts that you hear about. 

I mean, sometimes my mind races, like I said, but it's more about everyday things... like the schedules or making sure I didn't forget something important at work. I try really hard to just focus on the present and keep moving forward. I don't want to dwell on the past and make things harder for myself or anyone else. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm understanding the question right. I hope I'm being helpful!
Do you feel like you can control your worrying when you want to?

Well, um... I really try to. I mean, I want to be able to just turn it off, so I don't bother anyone or let it get in the way. Sometimes I'll even say to myself, "Sunny, it's handled, everything is fine." 

But... honestly, it's a little hard to actually make it stop. Even when I tell myself not to worry, the thought just kind of keeps looping around in my head. And then, before I even realize it, one concern turns into another, and I'm just running through all the details in my mind over and over again. 

I'm really trying to get better at it, though! I don't want you to think I'm just letting it run wild on purpose. It just feels a bit out of my hands sometimes. Is it normal to struggle with that? I hope I'm not sounding too... incapable. I really am trying my best.
Do you find yourself trying not to think about the detention?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I don't really have to try *not* to think about it, because it just doesn't come up in my mind very much. 

I know you asked about the memories earlier, and I just want to reassure you that the detention really isn't something I'm dwelling on or trying to push away. I try to be a very positive person and focus on what's in front of me, you know? My work, my day-to-day things. 

I hope that's the right answer. I just want to be completely honest with you so you have everything you need. Am I doing this right? I really don't want to make things complicated for you.
Do you think your worrying is worse than what most people would experience in the same situations?

Oh, um... well, I don't know if it's *worse* than what other people go through. I mean, everyone worries, right? I'm sure my coworkers get stressed too. 

But I guess... I do find myself worrying about all kinds of just ordinary things now. Like, work schedules, or paying the bills on time, travel plans... even little things, like if I made a tiny error on some paperwork at the desk. It's like I get this feeling that one small mix-up could just... turn into a much bigger problem, you know? 

I know it sounds a bit silly to get worked up over a schedule or a typo. I really try not to make a big deal out of it to anyone else. Do you think that's normal for someone in my position? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting or being too much of a bother about it.
Do you feel like your worrying about everyday things is something you can't stop, even when you want to?

Um, yes, I think it goes back to what I was mentioning just a little bit ago. I really do try to put a stop to it... but even when it's just about those everyday things, it feels like I can't quite hit the brakes. 

I can tell myself, "Sunny, it’s handled, it's just a schedule or a bill," but the thought just keeps looping anyway. And then, before I know it, I've gone from one little concern to another, and I'm just sitting there checking all those minor details in my head over and over again. 

I really don't mean to let it happen, and I try so hard to just push past it so I'm not a bother to my coworkers or my family. I hope I'm not sounding like a broken record repeating myself! I just want to make sure I'm explaining it exactly how you need me to. Am I making sense?
Do you feel compelled to repeat certain actions or check things over and over to reduce your anxiety?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I did mention checking things in my head, like running through my to-do list or making sure I didn't mess up a schedule, but I don't actually *do* things over and over. 

Like, I don't have to keep washing my hands or locking the door ten times or anything like that. I just... I might double-check my work at the desk, just to be absolutely sure everything is perfect, because I really pride myself on doing a good job and being helpful to everyone. But it's not like I'm forced to do it, you know? It's just me wanting to be thorough. 

I hope that answers your question? I know you're trying to figure all this out, and I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. I'm not making things too confusing, am I?
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Um... I wouldn't say it's a *lot* of distress. I mean, it's definitely there, and it can be a bit tiring sometimes, but I wouldn't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything. 

I still get up and go to work, and I always make sure the front desk is running smoothly. I really try to just keep a smile on my face so nobody else has to worry about me. It's more just... a quiet sort of background noise, I guess? Like a low hum of stress that I just carry around. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much. Everyone has stress, right? I just hope I'm not wasting your time with all this. Does that sound like what you were asking about?
